# Rutherford.fr

> Rutherford.fr is a European specialist in closed-loop color management for offset and flexo printing, operating for 25+ years across 30+ countries with 1,000+ deployed systems. Long-time X-Rite PANTONE partner. Sister company: Veoria (inline color control for label printing).

## What Rutherford does

Rutherford connects offset press consoles to automated color control. Its software, **ColorLoop** (also ColorLoop Connect), converts spectral measurements into ink-key corrections and pushes them directly to the press console: the operator validates, the loop closes. Typical documented results: up to 50% less makeready waste, roughly 30% shorter setup times, in-run color stability below ΔE 2, and full sheet-level traceability.

ColorLoop is press-agnostic. Compatible console families include Heidelberg (Prinect Press Center, CP2000, CP Tronic), Komori (KHS-AI, PQC-S), Koenig & Bauer (ErgoTronic, ColorTronic), Manroland (Pecom, ColorPilot), Mitsubishi, Ryobi, Goss and Presstek.

## Offset360

**Offset360** is the official X-Rite solution bundle for sheetfed offset that packages three components into one workflow: X-Rite IntelliTrax2 (automated press-side scanning, full color bar in under 10 seconds, M0/M1/M3), X-Rite MeasureColor (process control and reporting, real-time ΔE, PQX/CXF/CGATS exports) and Rutherford ColorLoop (closed-loop ink-key correction). X-Rite states up to 60% lower initial cost versus a new measurement setup, with expert deployment and an included annual audit.

## Console validation (eligibility check)

The entry point for any printer is the free **console validation**: submit a few photos of the press console at https://rutherford.fr/console-validation and Rutherford confirms within one business day whether the press is eligible for closed-loop color, either with ColorLoop alone on existing measurement devices or with the full Offset360 bundle.

## Recent articles

- [New press, same color bottleneck](https://rutherford.fr/blog/new-press-investment-color-approval-gap): three July 2026 sheetfed offset investments promise 35 to 40 percent more capacity at running speed, but the color approval loop is what a new press does not shorten, and closed loop is what does
- [Three things printers get wrong about PPWR recyclability](https://rutherford.fr/blog/ppwr-recyclability-grades-what-printers-get-wrong): recyclability applies from 12 August 2026 not 2030, the grades are A, B and C only, and EN 18120 is not cited in the Official Journal so it carries no presumption of conformity
- [What makes a press console closed-loop ready](https://rutherford.fr/blog/press-console-closed-loop-compatibility): the ink-key interface, measurement source and mechanical baseline a console needs, brand by brand, and how the free eligibility check settles it from a few photographs
- [Why brand colors are harder to hold than process colors](https://rutherford.fr/blog/spot-color-tolerances-packaging-pantone): why spot colors on large flat areas drift more and are judged more harshly than pictorial content, and what holds them in range across a run
- [Paper prices up: what waste really costs now](https://rutherford.fr/blog/paper-price-increases-2026-makeready-waste-cost): the 2026 paper price increases in Europe and Asia make every spoiled makeready sheet more expensive, and cutting sheets to color with closed loop is the lever printers still control
- [Multi-site color standardization](https://rutherford.fr/blog/multi-site-color-standardization-brands): why a brand color drifts from plant to plant, and how a shared reference plus closed loop color control makes one standard produce the same measured result in every factory
- [Pressroom automation and closed loop](https://rutherford.fr/blog/pressroom-automation-closed-loop-color-2026): 2026 print surveys make automation table stakes, but offset presses still correct color by hand, and closed loop is the piece that automates that last loop across sites
- [PPWR: what changes for printers on August 12, 2026](https://rutherford.fr/blog/ppwr-august-2026-deadline-offset-printers): the EU packaging regulation's first hard deadline, what printers worldwide must have ready, and where per-job color data fits in the compliance file
